html:
In 863 the brothers Constantine, later known as Cyril, and Methodius, two Byzantine monks from Thessalonica, arrived in Great Moravia as missionaries to the Slavs. They are honoured as the Apostles to the Slavs.

Prince Rastislav of Moravia had asked Emperor Michael III for teachers who could preach in the Slavic tongue, partly to limit the power of Frankish priests from East Francia. Thessalonica had many Slavic speakers, and the brothers knew the language. Constantine created the Glagolitic script, and they translated the gospels and the liturgy into what is now called Old Church Slavonic.

Frankish bishops objected to worship in any language but Latin, Greek or Hebrew. The brothers went to Rome, where the pope approved the Slavic liturgy. Constantine became a monk as Cyril and died there in 869. Methodius came back as archbishop but was jailed for a time by Frankish bishops, and after his death in 885 his followers were expelled. They took their work to Bulgaria, which led to the Cyrillic script and the Bulgarian church, and from there to the Rus'.
sum: In 863 the brothers Constantine, later known as Cyril, and Methodius, two Byzantine monks from Thessalonica, arrived in Great Moravia as missionaries to the Slavs. They are honoured as the Apostles to the Slavs.
